title: Qualify a Rust class-group mathematical core
objective: Implement the Rust class-group core qualification plan through complete native and browser evidence, preserving Sage.js public semantics, proof authority, portability, and measured PARI comparisons

oracles: Independent exact relation, ideal, transformation, generator, and completion certificates
Existing Sage.js dynamic class-group and class-unit contracts
exceptions: This campaign evaluates attributed handwritten Rust mathematical algorithms as an explicit, receipt-gated architecture exception rather than source-transparent lowering of an ordinary Python body.

handoff.summary: R0/W0 foundations now include strict contracts, pinned PARI controls, a frozen answer-free candidate generator, reproducible GMP/MPFR/MPC Wasm routes in three browsers, checked GMP Smith retry, arbitrary-precision HNF/SNF transforms, validated cubic preparation, presentation class maps, and a bounded row-6 diagnostic. These are qualification components, not a complete class-group backend.
risks: The current faithful fast path is authenticated only for H1 and does not yet provide a general prepared-field computation or public completion certificate.
The first Wasm class candidate is fast in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit but remains a relation-presentation candidate, not a completed class group.
The current row-6 diagnostic uses the equation order because the public experimental boundary cannot yet carry its denominator-three maximal-order basis.
next_steps: Finish the balanced private 60-open plus 60-held-out corpus without committing held-out answers.
Profile and replace the row-6 initial-cache bottleneck, then carry neutral maximal-order data into the fast relation loop.
Implement relation principal elements, units, regulator/completion authority, saturation, generator ideals, and the public Sage.js adapter.
